title: A flag-curve proof of an original-side pedal-area invariant
verdict: PASS for the signed-area product along elliptic billiard families whose least period is divisible by four.

proof: The ordered-endpoint flag cover branches simply at the four common tangents and has genus one. The billiard shift preserves holomorphic differential and is a primitive translation. Real-circle orientation and the central involution imply central inversion is the half-period for primitive even cycles, including star winding.

At each heading-at-infinity orbit point, the original area has no simultaneous adjacent vertex poles; hence it has at most a simple pole. The apparent double pole of a foot is multiplied by its vanishing neighboring difference, leaving at most a simple pole of the pedal area.

Write N=2m with m even. The two orbit pole sets are disjoint via the impossible congruence 2j=m−1 mod 2m. Invariant reversal provides complementary zeros at the potential simple poles. The product is holomorphic on the compact curve, so constant. The proof never divides by either area.

primary.claim: RGK's two checked table editions give the signed original-side product for even billiards; the source note correctly specifies least/primitive period as needed for the theorem.
Earlier equivalent theorem and mechanism for complex pedal points are explicitly credited.
